correctness.rationale: The proof derives the invariant homogeneous-petal state space and exact first-step harmonic equations for every s,m>=1 and r>0. Solving their geometric increment recurrence and the one-heterogeneous-petal first event proves all three fixation formulas. The neutral and finite-weak-selection algebra is explicit; fixed-fitness limits follow from a geometric sum and Taylor expansion, with no exchange of r and m limits. Exact-rational verifier passed 22400 identities and independent full-state/reduced-chain Markov checks passed 13677 comparisons; neither grid is treated as proof of the infinite-parameter claim.

originality.rationale: The first-public 2023 Liu–Masuda source defines the same model-1 group-copy rule but analyzes a 3-uniform hyperstar with every leaf pair, not edge-disjoint petals. Its transition counts do not imply the disjoint-petal two-parameter geometric harmonic system. The 2024 multilayer comparison uses pairwise interlayer competition, and the 2012 game model uses pairwise strategy replacement rather than whole-group copying. Actual published-research and historical-claim searches found no dominating theorem. This is best-knowledge novelty, not a priority certification.

value.rationale: This is the first tractable all-fitness calculation for the disjoint-petal higher-order reproductive analogue of a star in the inspected literature. The exact group-size boundary changes a star amplifier to a Moran-limit model at 3-person edges and to suppressor-like asymptotics at larger edges, while simultaneously quantifying hub/periphery reproductive asymmetry and finite-size weak-selection effects. The arbitrary s,m,r structural reduction and 3-size boundary are biologically motivated and more informative than a one-off computation.
